title: BridgeVLA++ Adds Spatio-Temporal Memory to 3D VLA Manipulation
summary: Researchers from CASIA's NLPR and ByteDance Seed posted BridgeVLA++ to arXiv on August 5, 2026, extending their NeurIPS 2025 BridgeVLA model with a unified spatio-temporal memory architecture for 3D manipulation. The added memory module lets the vision-language-action model reason over past observations and interaction history while preserving the original BridgeVLA's data efficiency and generalization, which come from aligning point-cloud inputs and predicted heatmaps with a pre-trained vision-language model. The team reports state-of-the-art results on two memory-dependent manipulation benchmarks without sacrificing performance on BridgeVLA's original spatial manipulation tasks. BridgeVLA++ is also validated on bimanual manipulation and on an additional real-world robot platform beyond the original paper's setup.
whyItMatters: Most VLA manipulation models react to a single snapshot of the scene, which breaks down on tasks that require remembering where an object was placed or what happened earlier in a sequence; adding explicit memory to an already data-efficient VLA is a step toward robots that handle longer, more realistic household and industrial tasks without retraining from scratch for every new environment.
